01.text: Open **http://10.1.20.15:8000** in a browser and log in with your Splunk account.

02.text: On the home page, click **Lab Security** in the Apps list. It opens the **Lab Security Overview** dashboard.

03.text: **1** Time range: last 24 hours by default; change it to look further back. **2** Host: show the Windows panels for one server only. **3** Hosts reporting should be **9** and green. **4** Alerts fired: above 0 turns red; check the alerts (steps 9 to 11).

04.text: **1** Forwarder status: every server should be **OK**. **SILENT** means nothing received for 15 minutes (server off, forwarder stopped, or network). **2** Recent alerts: newest first.

05.text: **1** Network devices (scroll the table right to see **status**): each should be **OK**. **QUIET** = no logs for 48 hours, **NEVER** = not sending logs yet. **2** Scribbler bridge must show **ok**. **3** Recent network alerts (LAB NET).

06.text: **1** Network configuration changes: who changed what on a switch or firewall. Each should be planned work you know about. **2** Switch events by type (logins, links, config). **3** Top denied sources: addresses the firewalls blocked most.

07.text: Windows activity: **1** failed logons, **2** new users and group changes. (Shown for the last 7 days; on a quiet day these panels say *No results found*, which is normal.)

08.text: **1** RDP and console logons, **2** newly installed services. Look for accounts, sources or times you do not expect.

09.text: Click the **Activity** icon at the top, then **Triggered Alerts**.

10.text: Check **App** shows **Lab Security**: the list then has the LAB, LAB NET and ESCU alerts, newest on top. Click **View Results** to see what fired an alert. Do not use **Edit Alert** or **Delete**.

11.text: The results open in a new tab: the time, the device or host, and what happened. Compare it with planned work; tell the lab operator about anything unexpected.

12.text: Click **Search** in the left bar. Type a search that starts with `index=`, pick the time range, press **Enter**. Example: everything switch SW-Ops (192.168.30.30) logged in the last 24 hours.

13.text: Each event shows its time and message. Click a field on the left, such as **host**, to see its values; click a value to narrow the search.

title: Splunk Daily Operations Guide
intro: How to check the lab's security monitoring each day. Everything here is read-only: it does not change Splunk.
subtitle: Lab SIEM: DMZH1_SIEM 10.1.20.15  |  Splunk Enterprise 10.6

table: Windows event logs: logons, accounts, services, PowerShell, Defender
Process starts, network connections, file and registry activity
Switch and firewall logs: logins, links, config changes, denied traffic

bullets: **Times in Splunk are UTC.** Lab local time is UTC + 8 hours (06:00 in Splunk = 14:00 local).
Alerts are checked every 5 minutes (ESCU every hour). There is no e-mail: alerts only show in Splunk.
This guide only looks at data. Nothing in it changes Splunk.

numbered: Open the **Lab Security Overview** dashboard (steps 1 and 2).
**Hosts reporting** shows **9** and every forwarder is **OK** (steps 3 and 4).
Every network device is **OK** and the Scribbler bridge shows **ok** (step 5).
**Alerts fired** is **0**, or open each new alert (steps 9 to 11).
Skim config changes, failed logons, account changes and logons for anything unexpected (steps 6 to 8).
Write down anything odd and tell the lab operator.

table: Hosts reporting below 9, or a host **SILENT**
Server off or restarting, forwarder stopped, or network path down
Check the server is running. Still silent after 15 minutes: tell the operator.
Device off, logging off, or the path to Scribbler broken. Quiet switches log very little, so QUIET can be normal
Tell the operator if it stays QUIET for more than a day.
Network logs are no longer reaching Splunk
Open it (steps 9 to 11). Planned work: note it. Otherwise tell the operator.
A config change you did not expect
Someone changed a switch or firewall
Note device, user and time; tell the operator.

items.p: Paste into **Search**, set the time range, press **Enter**.

table: Everything from one network device (by IP)
index=netdev sourcetype=scalance:syslog | stats count by netdev_name event_class
Switch events by device and type
index=wineventlog `lab_win(Security)` EventCode=4625 | `lab_failed_logon_fields` | stats count by host user src reason
Failed logons: who, from where, why
index=sysmon host=DMZH1MSSQL | stats count by EventCode
Sysmon activity on one server (1 = process start, 3 = network)

bullets: Edit, disable or delete alerts, dashboards or triggered alerts.
Restart Splunk or a forwarder. Tell the operator instead.
Search **All time** without a reason: it is slow. Last 24 hours or 7 days is enough.
Forget `index=`: without it a search finds nothing.
